domain_restrictions: g is an integer with g ≥ 2
genus g refers to genus of a numerical semigroup, hence typically g ≥ 0 (implicitly required so that N(g), N(g−1), N(g−2) are well-defined as counts of genus-specific semigroups)
N(k) must be meaningful for k = g, g−1, g−2 under the given restriction on g
root_semantic_sketch.normalized_claim: For all integers g ≥ 2, the number of numerical semigroups of genus g satisfies N(g) ≥ N(g−1) + N(g−2).

variables.name: N(g)
variables.role: counts numerical semigroups of genus g

payload.theorem_nl: Let N(g) denote the number of numerical semigroups of genus g. Prove that N(g) ≥ N(g−1) + N(g−2) for every integer g ≥ 2.

assembly_plan.proof_skeleton_nl: Fix an integer g >= 2. Use the semigroup-tree identity to rewrite N(g) as the number of effective-generator incidences over genus g-1 semigroups. Inside that incidence set, isolate the canonical pair (S, F(S)+m(S)) attached to each genus g-1 semigroup; there are exactly N(g-1) such pairs. Then apply the bottleneck injection to obtain at least N(g-2) further incidences in genus g-1 whose generators are explicitly noncanonical. Because canonical and noncanonical incidences are disjoint, the total number of incidences is at least the sum N(g-1)+N(g-2). Translating back through the semigroup-tree identity yields exactly N(g) >= N(g-1)+N(g-2).

steps.derives: For the given integer g >= 2, if we put h = g-1, then the set E_{g-1} of effective-generator incidences over genus-(g-1) numerical semigroups has cardinality |E_{g-1}| = N(g).
steps.trivial_justification: Apply L1 with h = g-1. Since g >= 2, we have g-1 >= 1 and in particular g-1 >= 0, so the lemma applies.

steps.derives: For h = g-1, the canonical-incidence set C_{g-1} is a subset of E_{g-1} and has cardinality |C_{g-1}| = N(g-1).
steps.trivial_justification: L2 says that for each genus-(g-1) numerical semigroup S, the element F(S)+m(S) is an effective generator. L3 packages this into the set-theoretic statement that C_{g-1} ⊆ E_{g-1} and |C_{g-1}| = N(g-1).

steps.derives: For h = g-1, the noncanonical-incidence set B_{g-1} satisfies |B_{g-1}| >= N(g-2).
steps.trivial_justification: Apply L4 with h = g-1. Because g >= 2, we have h = g-1 >= 1, so there exists an injection from genus-(g-2) numerical semigroups into B_{g-1}. Therefore the cardinality of B_{g-1} is at least N(g-2).

steps.derives: The full incidence set E_{g-1} satisfies |E_{g-1}| >= N(g-1) + N(g-2).
steps.trivial_justification: L5 gives |E_{g-1}| >= |C_{g-1}| + |B_{g-1}| because C_{g-1} and B_{g-1} are disjoint subsets of E_{g-1}. Substituting the values from A2 and the lower bound from A3 yields |E_{g-1}| >= N(g-1) + N(g-2).
From A1, N(g) = |E_{g-1}|. From A4, |E_{g-1}| >= N(g-1) + N(g-2). By substitution, N(g) >= N(g-1) + N(g-2).

context_items.content: A numerical semigroup is a subset S of the nonnegative integers N = {0,1,2,...} such that 0 is in S, S is closed under addition, and N \ S is finite.
context_items.label: numerical_semigroup

context_items.content: For a numerical semigroup S, its genus g(S) is the cardinality of N \ S. If g(S) > 0, its Frobenius number F(S) is the largest integer not in S. Its multiplicity m(S) is the smallest positive integer in S.
context_items.label: genus_frobenius_multiplicity

context_items.content: For a numerical semigroup S, an element x in S \ {0} is a minimal generator if x cannot be written as a+b with positive a,b in S. If g(S) > 0, an effective generator of S means a minimal generator x with x > F(S).
context_items.label: minimal_and_effective_generator

lemmas.statement_nl: For every integer h >= 0, let E_h be the set of pairs (S,x) such that S is a numerical semigroup of genus h and x is an effective generator of S. Then E_h has cardinality N(h+1). Equivalently, the number of numerical semigroups of genus h+1 equals the total number of effective generators among all numerical semigroups of genus h. A concrete bijection is: from (S,x) in E_h, send it to the child semigroup S \ {x}; conversely, from a numerical semigroup T of genus h+1, send it to (T ∪ {F(T)}, F(T)).
lemmas.strictly_easier_reason: It is a structural counting identity from the semigroup tree and does not yet compare two different genus counts.

lemmas.role_in_assembly: This identifies a canonical effective generator attached to each positive-genus semigroup.
lemmas.self_check_notes: The statement defines all nonstandard quantities locally and does not rely on other lemmas.

lemmas.statement_nl: Let S be a numerical semigroup with positive genus, Frobenius number F(S), and multiplicity m(S). Then the element F(S)+m(S) belongs to S, is a minimal generator of S, and is greater than F(S). Therefore F(S)+m(S) is an effective generator of S.
lemmas.strictly_easier_reason: It is a local fact about one semigroup, not a global counting inequality across all semigroups of a fixed genus.

lemmas.role_in_assembly: This counts the canonical effective-generator incidences: exactly one for each genus-h semigroup.

lemmas.statement_nl: For every integer h >= 1, let C_h be the set of pairs (S, F(S)+m(S)) where S is a numerical semigroup of genus h, F(S) is its Frobenius number, and m(S) is its multiplicity. Then C_h has cardinality N(h). Moreover, by the fact that F(S)+m(S) is an effective generator, C_h is a subset of the set E_h of all pairs (S,x) with S a numerical semigroup of genus h and x an effective generator of S.
lemmas.strictly_easier_reason: It is a bookkeeping statement once the canonical generator F(S)+m(S) is known.

lemmas.bottleneck_reason: Constructing such an injection is the essential global combinatorial content beyond the basic semigroup-tree identity; once this is available, the Fibonacci-type lower bound follows by disjoint counting.
lemmas.role_in_assembly: This is the extra-count bottleneck that provides at least N(h-1) noncanonical effective-generator incidences in genus h.

variables.name: B_h

lemmas.statement_nl: For every integer h >= 1, let B_h be the set of pairs (S,x) such that S is a numerical semigroup of genus h, x is an effective generator of S, and x is not equal to F(S)+m(S), where F(S) is the Frobenius number and m(S) is the multiplicity of S. Then there exists an injective map from the set of numerical semigroups of genus h-1 into B_h. Equivalently, the number of such noncanonical effective-generator incidences in genus h is at least N(h-1).

lemmas.role_in_assembly: This turns the canonical count and the injected noncanonical count into a single lower bound for the total number of effective-generator incidences.
lemmas.self_check_notes: All sets are explicitly defined within the statement; the lemma is self-contained.

lemmas.statement_nl: For every integer h >= 1, let E_h be the set of all pairs (S,x) where S is a numerical semigroup of genus h and x is an effective generator of S. Let C_h be the subset of pairs (S, F(S)+m(S)) with S of genus h. Let B_h be the subset of pairs (S,x) where S has genus h, x is an effective generator of S, and x != F(S)+m(S). Then C_h and B_h are disjoint subsets of E_h, and therefore |E_h| >= |C_h| + |B_h|.
lemmas.strictly_easier_reason: It is a purely set-theoretic disjoint-union counting step and contains no semigroup-tree difficulty.

candidates.strategy_summary: Use the numerical-semigroup tree. Count genus-(h+1) semigroups by effective generators of genus-h semigroups, then split effective generators into one canonical generator F(S)+m(S) for each genus-h semigroup plus a second disjoint family of noncanonical effective generators supplied by an injective bottleneck construction from genus-(h-1) semigroups.
